newsitem.title: USA: Kennecott, unions say no to Utah strike.
newsitem.headline: Kennecott, unions say no to Utah strike.

text.p: There will be no strike at Kennecott Copper in Utah in the event of a failure to reach a new labor deal by midnight Sept. 30 local time, the company and the labor unions said in a joint statement.
"No strike will occur tonight. The parties will continue to negotiate and they are optimistic about the settlement." said Jack Golden, union negotiator and Ron Skaer of Kennecott in their statement.
Golden is director of the United Steelworkers of America and Skaer is a Kennecott human resourses official.
The present three-year labor contract covers 1,800 employees at the 310,000 short tons per year refinery in Utah, one of the largest in the world.
Both sides were locked in talks over the weekend and have agreed on minor issues but not on salary demands.
